root_idea.summary: The root expresses agitation, disturbance, or turbulent movement in something.
root_idea.development: This principle is applied literally to waves and surging water, and extended to confused movement among people and to disturbed affairs. The Quranic verb preserves the wave-like sense of turbulent motion.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form مَاجَ rather than the attested imperfect يَمُوجُ.
Displayed as the Quranic collective noun مَوْجٌ.

senses.definition: To surge or move in turbulent commotion; to intermingle confusedly.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction يَمُوجُ فِي بَعْضٍ, people move and intermingle turbulently with one another.

senses.definition: A wave, waves, billows, or surges; water rising above other water.
senses.usage_conditions: The collective noun may be rendered in the singular or plural according to context. It is used literally for water waves and metaphorically for successive or layered waves, including waves of darkness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be agitated, tumultuous, or confused; of the sea, waves, things, affairs, or people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Classical figurative uses include an affair becoming confused, a person becoming perplexed, and people becoming discordant or disturbed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To decline from the truth or from the true, right, or just course.
To move back and forth or from side to side between the skin and the bone or flesh, said of the kneecap or a ganglion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical usage describing mobile movement beneath or between bodily tissues.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A swift she-camel whose foregirth thongs have shifted because of the backward and forward motion of her gait.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of a female camel, defined by the movement caused by its gait.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wave-tossed, agitated, or tumultuous; especially a sea in commotion, and also a man in agitation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Adjectival derivatives describing turbulent motion; مَوَّاجٌ is an intensive description of a sea tumultuous with waves.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An imitative echo-word in the fixed expression فَرَسٌ غَوْجٌ مَوْجٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized idiomatic use in which مَوْجٌ is described as an imitative sequent rather than the ordinary wave noun.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Covers general agitation of the sea, waves, things, and disturbed affairs.
Generalized use for anything in commotion.
Agitation and perplexity of an individual.
People in commotion; the Quranic and broader classical branches are both covered.
People in a discordant and disturbed state.
Distinct figurative use with عَنْ to decline from the right course.
Pointer-only cross-reference to the Form I entry.
Wave, billow, surge, and water-rising sense.
Figurative expression for the prime of youth.
Intensive adjectival description of a sea tumultuous with waves.
Agitated man use of the adjective.

cautions: The Quranic verb is attested as the imperfect يَمُوجُ, but the public headword is normalized to the standard perfect citation form مَاجَ. The noun مَوْجٌ is used both literally for water waves and metaphorically in the layered-wave imagery of 24:40.
